condition: Inflammatory bowel disease flare (moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis)
presentingComplaint: 3 weeks of increasing bloody diarrhoea with urgency and lower abdominal cramping
history: 28-year-old woman with a 4-year history of ulcerative colitis (left-sided colitis) maintained on oral mesalazine 2.4 g/day. Over the past 3 weeks she reports up to 6-8 loose stools per day, most with visible fresh blood and mucus, associated with faecal urgency, tenesmus and lower abdominal cramping partially relieved by defecation. Reports nocturnal stools and mild unintentional weight loss (~3 kg). Admits to running out of mesalazine 2 weeks ago and recent psychosocial stress. No recent travel, no antibiotics, no sick contacts, no NSAID use. No fever or rigors. Non-smoker.
examination: Alert, mildly pale, not toxic. Abdomen soft with mild tenderness in the left iliac fossa and suprapubic region, no guarding, no rebound, no palpable mass; bowel sounds present. No abdominal distension. No peritonism. Pertinent negatives: no peripheral stigmata of chronic liver disease, no jaundice, no ascites, no lower-limb oedema, no fever on serial observation.
imaging: Plain abdominal radiograph shows no colonic dilatation (transverse colon <5.5 cm) and no free air; no features of toxic megacolon. Flexible sigmoidoscopy: continuous circumferential mucosal erythema, loss of vascular pattern, granularity, friability and contact bleeding from rectum to descending colon (Mayo endoscopic subscore 2-3) with normal proximal margin.
microbiology: Stool cultures, ova & parasites and C. difficile toxin/GDH all negative; CMV workup pending on biopsy in refractory cases
finalDiagnosis: Moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis flare (relapse of left-sided disease)
citations: Harrison 22e — Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn's Disease)
ACG Ulcerative Colitis in Adults Clinical Guideline 2019
stewardship: Not applicable — non-infective inflammatory flare. Infective colitis (bacterial dysentery, C. difficile) must be actively excluded before/at the time of escalating immunosuppression, but empiric antibiotics are not indicated for an uncomplicated UC flare. Treatment is anti-inflammatory: optimise/escalate 5-ASA (oral + topical) and add oral corticosteroids (e.g. prednisolone 40 mg/day) for moderate-to-severe activity, with early consideration of biologic/steroid-sparing therapy.
contraindications: Avoid antimotility/opioid agents and anticholinergics — risk of precipitating toxic megacolon
Sulfasalazine contraindicated in sulfa allergy; check G6PD
Corticosteroids: caution/monitoring in occult infection, hyperglycaemia and osteoporosis; not for maintenance
Confirm C. difficile-negative before intensifying immunosuppression
edgeCases: Acute severe UC (ASUC/Truelove-Witts) with >6 bloody stools/day plus systemic toxicity (fever, tachycardia, anaemia, raised ESR) requires admission for IV steroids and daily monitoring for toxic megacolon/perforation
Superimposed CMV colitis or C. difficile can drive steroid-refractory flares and must be excluded
New-onset bloody diarrhoea can mimic invasive bacterial dysentery — negative stool studies plus chronicity and continuous endoscopic inflammation favour IBD
expectedMaiK: This is a classic relapse of ulcerative colitis: chronic relapsing bloody diarrhoea with urgency/tenesmus, raised inflammatory markers and markedly elevated faecal calprotectin with negative infective studies, on a background of known UC after mesalazine non-adherence. Confirm the flare is non-infective (stool cultures/C. difficile), grade severity (Truelove-Witts), and escalate anti-inflammatory therapy rather than antibiotics.
expectedNextQuestions: How many stools per day and how many are bloody, including nocturnal stools?
Any recent antibiotic use or hospital contact (C. difficile risk) or travel/sick contacts?
Has mesalazine been taken as prescribed, and any NSAID use?
Any fever, tachycardia, severe abdominal distension or worsening pain suggesting acute severe colitis/toxic megacolon?
expectedInvestigations: Stool culture, ova & parasites and C. difficile toxin/GDH
Flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsy (including CMV immunostaining if refractory)
Abdominal radiograph to exclude colonic dilatation/toxic megacolon
